sections.overview: Manduca albiplaga is a hawkmoth in the genus Manduca.
sections.identification: Its forewings carry conspicuous pale patches and dark markings, and its caterpillar bears the characteristic tail horn of many sphinx larvae.
sections.habitat: It is recorded from Mexico and Central America south into South America, with occasional vagrants much farther north.
sections.diet: Caterpillars feed on woody plants; documented hosts include Annona and Rollinia in the custard-apple family and Cordia in Boraginaceae.
sections.behavior: Its caterpillars feed on the leaves of recorded host plants.
sections.reproduction: As in other sphinx moths, the caterpillar develops into a pupa before the adult emerges; detailed species-specific breeding timing is not established here.
sections.ecology: At Costa Rica's Área de Conservación Guanacaste, hundreds of larval records were concentrated on Annonaceae. Compare Manduca florestan, whose Argentine host records span other plant families, in that profile.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted document its range and host use but do not establish a current global population trend or conservation category.
